pr_title: Update the filtering logic to properly handle directories with `.gdignore` files

issue_context.title: [3.2.4 rc1] Engine crashes on export when having Android custom build in the project folder
issue_context.body:
Godot version:
3.2.4 rc1

OS/device including version:
Windows 10

Issue description:
Engine crashes on export (no matter to which platform) when having Android custom build in the project folder. Nothing special shows on the system console when it crashes. Have to delete the "android" folder to get it work. This only happens after several successful exports using the custom build and can be avoided by reinstalling the custom build template. I had not experienced this until I started using 3.2.4 rc1.

Steps to reproduce:
This issue is quite hard to reproduce. I only encountered it twice when working on my project. But considering the the release date of rc1 is not very long ago, I doubt it is just an individual case. I report this in case others also bump into a similar issue.
comments: It didn't crash for me, i just had lot's of errors to relsove because some Gradle scripts and the Android Manifest changed. `GodotApp.java` also changed. Once i got it working i ran into #45606 though, which i can even reproduce with a simple empty project.

I have no problem getting my game signed (with debug key) and running on Android except for this irregular issue. And I found this issue appears more frequently when I use Deploy with Remote Debug instead of manually copying and installing the exported APK on my mobile. I switched back to beta6 to see if this is a regression issue.
@floppyhammer Thanks for reporting the issue. I'll take a look and attempt to reproduce it.

This also happens to 3.2.4.beta6.
![screen-record](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28705694/106697243-528b2b80-6619-11eb-98f3-e8f396304728.gif)

@floppyhammer There seems to be error logs in the output console in your recording. Can you provide these logs.

Also grab the following files:
- `manifest-merger*report` files from the `android/build/build/outputs/logs` directory
- `lint-results-*` files in the `android/build/build/reports` directory

@m4gr3d I don't see the `android/build/build/reports` directory.

The only errors in the Godot log file are related to Nakama.
[godot.log](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5949787/godot.log)

There's only one file in the `android/build/build/outputs/logs` directory.
[manifest-merger-debug-report.txt](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5949789/manifest-merger-debug-report.txt)
@floppyhammer Can you see if you can reproduce the issue in `3.2.3` stable. I'm trying to confirm whether this is a regression or whether it's a bug that had escaped our notice.
@m4gr3d Yes, I will.
@m4gr3d I don't think this issue is reproducible in `3.2.3.stable`. I switched back to stable and haven't met the issue yet developing on the same project.
@m4gr3d Yes, I know how to do it. But I have a question. If I build the editor from the current 3.2 branch, can I use it with the previously released rc2 export templates?

@floppyhammer You can but your built version will look for the templates in a `3.2.4.rc` directory whereas the rc2 export templates will be in a `3.2.4.rc2` directory.
You can easily fix that by copying the files from the `3.2.4.rc2` directory into the `3.2.4.rc` one.
@m4gr3d I did as you said, and the templates are now working. I will try to reproduce the issue.

@m4gr3d This is what it says when the engine crashes:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28705694/108374121-91d19300-723b-11eb-96da-d7afdcb2084a.png)
@floppyhammer Can you provide the full logs from the beginning of the build; it should start with `Exporting for Android...`.

@floppyhammer Also does this occur when you deploy with `remote debug` or for any export?
Do you have any `gradle.conf` or `AndroidManifest.conf` files in your project?

@m4gr3d Godot's file log got truncated somehow, but I managed to copy console content before it shut down.
[godot.log](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6006803/godot.log)
[console-output.txt](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6006814/console-output.txt)

It occurs as long as I use Android custom build. But it seems using `remote debug` increases the probability of occurrence. And once it occurs, it would crash the engine no matter which export I use or whether the `use_custom_build` option in Android export settings is enabled. The only solution is to delete the custom build or reinstall it.

No, I don't have those two files in my project. The `android` folder is automatically generated in my project when installing Android custom build, and I didn't add any other Android related file besides that.

Console output for Windows export:
[console-output-windows.txt](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6006844/console-output-windows.txt)

Console output for Android export when `use_custom_build` is disabled:
[console-output-android.txt](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6006848/console-output-android.txt)

@floppyhammer I've noticed this line in your log:
```
TODO_Manager: There was an error at: res://android/build/build/intermediates/compressed_assets/debug/out/assets/android/build/build/intermediates/merged_assets/debug/out/android/build/build/intermediates/merged_res_blame_folder/debug/out/multi-v2
```

This sounds similar to issue #42982. Can you remove the `android` folder once more, export a couple of times and provides the logs.
It seems the engine is somehow parsing the `android` folder as well when it shouldn't. The logs from successful exports should allow me to track down why the `android` folder is being included.

@m4gr3d 
[console-output-without-android-folder.txt](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6007561/console-output-without-android-folder.txt)
@floppyhammer Sorry I meant to reinstall the `android` folder then run a couple of times with custom build enabled.

@m4gr3d It's okay. Here.
[console-output-successful-exports.txt](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6007624/console-output-successful-exports.txt)

@m4gr3d Let me know if you need more info.
[console-output.txt](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6020300/console-output.txt)

@floppyhammer @HEAVYPOLY I'm able to reproduce the issue if I add in the Android export `include` section a file extension or filename contained in the `android` directory (e.g: `*.json`, `*.png`).

Do you have anything listed in the `include` section for your Android exports?
@m4gr3d Yes, I have `*.json` in the filters.

> @m4gr3d Yes, I have `*.json` in the filters.

That confirms the source of the issue then! The filter include logic disregards the `.gdignore` file and walk down the directory tree to fetch resources to be included. I'm preparing a pull request to update that so that it respects the `.gdignore` file.
I have .import and the entire android folder in the exclude filters, I think there were errors related to .import files in android custom build.
@floppyhammer @HEAVYPOLY Can you test #46336 and see if it addresses the issue you were seeing.

@m4gr3d I failed to cherry-pick #46336 as there were conflicts. Will it work if I just build from that branch?

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28705694/108808562-dd8c8f80-75e1-11eb-99d9-c2a23cdb06ce.png)

> Will it work if I just build from that branch?

@floppyhammer Yes, that will work.

> I have .import and the entire android folder in the exclude filters

Side note, but be aware that the `.import/` folder is meant to be included in the exported PCK, that's where all imported resources reside that your project actually needs. As long as you don't use *any* imported resource (PNG, WAV, etc.) like I think you do in Heavypaint it should be fine, but at the same time it's likely not necessary to exclude `.import/` as it shouldn't contain much (aside from `icon.png` maybe).
@m4gr3d As I exported dozens of times and haven't experienced a crash yet, I say you nailed it!

@floppyhammer Great to hear!

Can you also double-check in the logs that the export process doesn't attempt to save any files from the `android/build` directory.
@m4gr3d I can confirm it doesn't.
